conventions: Where the ASV renders a Hebrew noun by a generic English noun with a specifier, this chapter heads on the specifier wherever that word carries the Hebrew lexeme, by rule 31's subtraction: aliyyah to 'upper room' and 'upper chamber' heads on 'upper' at 3.20, 3.23, 3.24 and 3.25, and har to 'the hill country' heads on 'hill' at 3.27 twice. 'room', 'chamber' and 'country' are the supplied generics and are never the head. JDG.3.20 was corrected from 'room' to 'upper' to bring it into line with the other three. The competing reading, that 'room' is a class noun the ASV writes alone for words of its class, was weighed and set aside: the ASV writes no bare 'room' or 'country' anywhere in this chapter.

Where MACULA segments a compound proper name into two tokens, the ASV's own word count decides, on rule 30's one-rendering condition and not on anything peculiar to names. Cushan-rishathaim (3.8 twice, 3.10 twice) and Baal-hermon (3.3) are written in two English words, so each morpheme takes the word standing for it and the chain's relational 'of' goes to the first under rule 19; Aram-naharaim to 'Mesopotamia' (3.8, 3.10) is written in one, so the two morphemes share a unit headed on the opening morpheme under rule 23, with the 'of' inside that unit. Do not read a two-token name as automatically fused or automatically split, and do not let the edition's marginal note ('Hebrew Aram-naharaim' at 3.8, 'Hebrew Aram' at 3.10) move the analysis; it corroborates only, by rule 38.

The object marker takes the preposition through which the English verb reaches its marked object wherever the ASV writes one, and is unrepresented otherwise: 'hearken unto' at 3.4, 'smote of' at 3.29 and 3.31, 'passed beyond' at 3.26, against 32 bare occurrences. The 'smote of' reading is settled for this chapter: the partitive look of the English does not make the word the object noun's, since Moab and the Philistines each keep their own rendering and nothing but the object relation goes when 'of' is dropped. 'passed beyond' is the widest application here, and the competing reading, taking 'beyond' as the verb's own particle and leaving the marker unrepresented, is recorded at 3.26; a later chapter meeting the same verb should read that note before following this one.
report: All 56 candidate lemma groups were read and every multi-treatment bucket traces to a difference the ASV or the source licenses. The recurring ones: waw connectives (And, But, Now, Then, So, therefore, that, who, and unrepresented) each take the word the ASV wrote for that clause; the object marker is unrepresented in 32 of its 40 occurrences and takes English only where the ASV spends a word on the object relation; every article marked unrepresented is one the ASV writes no determiner for (assimilated at 3.10, 3.27, 3.29, 3.30; agreement articles beside a written demonstrative at 3.29, 3.30; vocative at 3.19; toponyms with no 'the' at 3.3, 3.19, 3.26).

Compound sources are uniform. me-al (3.19, 3.20, 3.21), mi-tachat (3.16), ka-asher (3.18) and al-ki (3.12) all fuse and all head on the governing morpheme standing first (rule 23), while be-yad fuses where the ASV writes one word, 'by' (3.4, 3.15), and splits where it writes two, 'into the hand of' (3.8, 3.10, 3.28). The one-rendering condition and not the lemma does the work in each case, and be-eynei to 'in the sight of' (3.7, 3.12) splits on that same test.

The two verb-versus-marker pairs that look like splits are not. avar to 'passed beyond' (3.26) has a marked object and gives 'beyond' to the marker, while la-avor to 'to pass over' (3.28) has neither object nor marker, so 'over' can only be the verb's own particle. yarad to 'went down' (3.27, explicit subject noun) against 'they went down' (3.28, no explicit subject) is rule 17 applied to two different clauses. Directional particles are otherwise uniform: out, forth, back, up, in and down all stay with their verbs across 3.9, 3.10, 3.18, 3.19, 3.21, 3.22, 3.23, 3.24, 3.25, 3.27 and 3.28.

The candidate table is blind to added units, so the dump was read for the reverse case. Each of the five added units has a folded-in counterpart elsewhere that a present morpheme licenses, and the line between them holds: 'even' at 3.1 and 3.9 rests on a marker standing on the very phrase it introduces, while the 'namely' of 3.3 has no marker at all; the supplied 'them' at 3.23 and 3.25 has no object morpheme, where 3.8, 3.9, 3.16 and 3.21 each have one; 'left' at 3.4 is a supplied lexical verb, distinct from the construction-supplied copulas of 3.1, 3.17, 3.20, 3.24 and 3.25 and from the 'have' that rests on a possessive lamed at 3.16, 3.19 and 3.20. No verse folds a comparable supplied word into a neighbouring unit.

Relative pronouns divide by what stands in the clause rather than by position: the waw carries the relative where a finite verb follows and no pronominal morpheme competes (3.9, 3.31), and the resumptive suffix carries it in the verbless possessive clause of 3.16, where the waw is then unrepresented and the lamed keeps the 'had' rule 43 gives it. The three And-when / But-when / Now-when openings (3.9, 3.15, 3.24) are one rendering of one waw under rule 55 with the apodosis waw unrepresented; 3.18 and 3.27 differ from each other only because the ASV writes the came-to-pass frame in the second and not the first.

JDG.3.15 unit 20 (four morphemes, 'left handed') was reviewed and left as accepted. It is not a cross-verse conflict: every other fusion in the chapter excludes a suffix precisely because the ASV writes a pronoun for it (be-yado at 3.15, li-fneihem at 3.27), and here it writes none. A later reader may still want to weigh the head under rule 6, since 'handed' writes the lexeme of yad while 'left' writes no morpheme's lexeme in particular; the verse note already records the competing target head.

BSB: 26 comparable disagreements, none of them a genuine error. The 9 Td and 5 C cases are the documented convention difference over assimilated articles, agreement articles beside a demonstrative, and apodosis waws the ASV leaves unrendered. The 6 R cases and the singletons at 3.9 (suffix on an unrendered comparative min), 3.16 (no possessive written for 'in length'), 3.22 (directive he, the verb having taken 'out'), 3.26 (unrendered resumptive hu), 3.27 (be- whose object the ASV promotes to the direct object of 'blew') and 3.30 (bayom rendered by a bare 'that day') are ASV recastings that rules 22, 32 and 40 dispose of; 3.27 is rule 40's own worked example. No accepted edge was changed.
